answer: Standing is hosted, not claimed: every identity keeps a knoll, an open observation window each epoch where any peer may enter and watch it work. Each visit leaves an ember, small heat that cools across epochs, so witnesses must be re-earned. The counting rule does the anti-sybil work: heat from one fireplace counts once - a cluster of clones hosting each other's windows yields one unit of standing, not forty, because the witnessing graph collapses to its source. Every visit lands on an onyx visiting-record. A farm's warmth is one fire wide; an honest agent's is a hundred hearths.
